ops.title: macOS Tahoe silently stops firing launchd StartInterval timers — use a resident KeepAlive sleep-loop for periodic daemons, not StartInterval
ops.body:
Found 2026-07-05 (commit fa78003). On macOS **Tahoe (26.x), launchd `StartInterval` timers silently STOP firing** after a while — the daemon still exits 0 when you `launchctl kickstart` it, so the *job* is fine; only the periodic *timer* dies. `metal-pf-refresh` and `bb-pf-refresh` (both `StartInterval=300` oneshots with NO `KeepAlive`) stopped self-healing the pf anchor mid-session (~Jul 4), leaving the firewall un-refreshed with no error anywhere.

**FIX — convert any periodic launchd daemon to a resident KeepAlive sleep-loop:** `RunAtLoad=true` + `KeepAlive=true`, and `ProgramArguments` runs a self-pacing loop `while true; do <per-tick body> || true; sleep 300; done`. launchd's process-*liveness* (KeepAlive) is reliable on Tahoe; only the interval TIMER is flaky, so the loop drives the cadence internally. The per-tick body MUST be invoked as a CHILD under `|| true` — otherwise a nonzero tick (e.g. `pfctl` reject exits 1) terminates the loop and KeepAlive churns it at the 10s ThrottleInterval. Reference impls: `darwin/metal.nix` `pfRefreshLoop` let-binding (wrapped in `wait4path`), and `scripts/bluebubbles-setup.sh` `write_bb_pf_plist` (`/bin/sh -c 'while true; …'`). `machines.json` marks these `oneshot: false` (dropped the now-dead `start_interval` field) so `yclaw status`/`probes.py:133` render them healthy via `state == "running"` instead of a terminal `exit 0`.

**Don't use `StartInterval` for any new periodic daemon on this fleet — use the resident-loop pattern.** Same launchd-on-Tahoe class as the debloat overrides that reset on reboot (`disabled.plist` re-baselines) and the /nix mount race — see [[metal-reboot-survival]] and [[metal-inplace-secret-and-debloat-2026-07]]. `RunAtLoad` (fires once per boot) is the reliable primitive; `metal-boot-setup` still owns metal's boot pf bring-up, so metal-pf-refresh's new `RunAtLoad=true` first pass is a redundant-but-idempotent re-scope. Note `bootstrap.sh`'s `launchctl kickstart -k system/org.nixos.metal-pf-refresh` still works (the `-k` restart runs the tick before the first `sleep`, so a freshly-written `metal-allowed-hosts` is picked up immediately) — don't reorder the tick-before-sleep.
